decisive_items: a 5 × 5 cm exophytic mass at the descending–sigmoid junction occupying half of the lumen
invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon consistent with intussusception
response.rationale: The presence of an exophytic mass and invagination of the descending colon into the sigmoid colon supports intussusception, although the mass could also suggest cancer.

rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence for diverticulitis beyond colicky pain and mucopurulent discharge.
While a polyp is possible, the size and description of the mass, along with other symptoms, make intussusception or cancer more likely.
